With one argument, `type(obj)` doesn't build a new class. It returns `Py_TYPE(obj)`, which is the existing type object, with its reference count incremented. On CPython 3.14 the interpreter often specializes this call (`CALL_TYPE_1`), so it never walks the MRO. The time doesn't depend on `d`, and the only allocation is a reference to an existing object.

TIME: O(1)
SPACE: O(1)
